_comment: Cost-tiering policy. Edit THIS file to change routing — not the code. Model IDs are examples; set to what you actually run. Tiers ascend in cost/capability; the router always picks the LOWEST tier a task needs.

t1.note: small/cheap: classify, extract, route, simple transforms

t3.note: frontier: planning, architecture, complex tests, hard review

limits._comment: Budget/rate circuit breaker — the kill switch's automatic twin. router/killswitch.js counts decisions in the audit ledger within a sliding window (windowMinutes) and refuses new requests once a ceiling is met — blocked:"circuit-open" — halting a runaway loop or cost blowout with no human at the console. Set a ceiling to null (or omit it) to disable that dimension; set windowMinutes<=0 to disable the breaker entirely.
limits._spend_note: NOTIONAL cost ceilings (USD) over the same sliding window. Subscription-billed runners do not spend this money — it is the comparable yardstick across tiers, and the ceiling a request COUNT cannot express (a t3 xhigh run costs orders of magnitude more than a t1 classify). Set null to disable. See AIOPS.md.

controls._maxTier_note: Hard ceiling. Set to 't2' to forbid frontier spend for a lane unless a request explicitly passes allowFrontier:true.
controls._override_note: If false, requests cannot force provider/model/tier — policy is absolute.

risk._comment: Agent risk = data-sensitivity x access(blast radius) x autonomy (NIST AI RMF / Databricks DASF consensus). Each request scores 1-3 per dimension; the derived level drives PROPORTIONAL controls. Dimensions come from the scope (data) and the request's `action`/`trigger` fields.

controlsByDimension._comment: Thresholds that switch each control on. requireApproval: a human must approve before the runner acts. requireVerify: force a fresh-context check. requireIsolation: confidential data must run in a siloed/dedicated runner. blockCrossVendor: don't send confidential work to a 2nd vendor (addresses M4).

enforce._isolation_note: warn|block. Keep 'warn' until the C1/C2 per-scope runners are cut over (phase 5); then set 'block'.

guardrails._comment: Prompt-injection & output guardrails (threat-model H3). router/guardrails.js is a HEURISTIC layer (not a guarantee) — the structural mitigation is C1 per-scope mounts + per-scope allowedTools. input: off|warn|block — 'warn' attaches inputScan findings to the decision and proceeds; 'block' refuses the request (blocked:'guardrail-input') when a finding meets minLevelToBlock. output: off|warn — 'warn' runs outputScan on the runner result and attaches decision.outputFindings. minLevelToBlock: low|medium|high — the lowest finding severity that blocks under input:'block'. Only finding TYPES reach the audit ledger, never the matched text. See GUARDRAILS.md.
guardrails._backend_note: heuristic (default; built-in regex, no network) | lakera | bedrock. When set to an ML backend, backendUrl must point at the detector; findings merge with the heuristic and fall back to it on any error. See DETECTION-BACKENDS.md.

modes._comment: Operating mode = who LEADS and who SUPPORTS. Orthogonal to risk (which sets control INTENSITY); mode sets the human/AI relationship. Framing follows Sol Rashidi's Executive AI Compass (c) 2025 (AI-only / AI-led+human-supported / human-led+AI-supported / human-only), mapped here onto enforceable controls. Set `mode` per scope (a deliberate per-function choice); a request may only make it MORE restrictive, never less. maxAction caps what the agent may DO; humanValidation: none | output (human validates the agent's output before it's authoritative — 'support' as substantive review) | actor (the human performs the action; the agent only assists).

approvers._comment: Approver RBAC + segregation of duties (threat-model M5). When a request arrives with approved:true, router/rbac.js checks the NAMED approver: their identityGroup must be authorized to approve at the request's risk level (byRisk) and, if the scope is explicitly listed (byScope), for that scope too; and for the risk levels in segregationOfDuties.riskLevels the approver must differ from the requester. Groups map to Google Groups (see scopes.json `identityGroup`). Every risk level MUST map to >=1 group — rbac.js fails closed otherwise. Identity is captured at the approval ingress and passed to the router as `approver`+`approverGroups` (see RBAC.md / n8n approval-gate meta).

byScope._comment: Optional per-scope narrowing applied ON TOP of byRisk. If a scope is listed, the approver must ALSO belong to one of these groups (never a relaxation). Use for ethical-wall / confidential scopes.

segregationOfDuties._comment: Risk levels at which the approver must be a different identity than the requester.
